thread:
sam: Quick heads-up — saw a reproducible perf regression after the recent NVIDIA driver bump. nsight sampling + timeline shows kernel-selection thrash and KV cache invalidations, overall ~18% token throughput drop. attaching snippets below.

sam: Repro notes: nsys run shows repeated launches of two different matmul kernels (fast vs compatibility fallback) for the same op across requests. KV cache entries get evicted around the same time. Looks like driver+cuBLAS chooses different kernel variants across contexts.

sam: nsys command we used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --output=/tmp/profile --sample=none 
  --stats=true --force-overwrite --target-processes=all ./run_inference.sh
```

sam: nsys output log excerpt:
```
[WARNING] CUPTI: could not initialize activity API (CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED)
[INFO] Timeline: kernel cuBLAS_SGEMM_..._fast 0.45ms
[INFO] Timeline: kernel cuBLAS_SGEMM_..._compat 0.82ms
[INFO] KVCache: evict key=chat-123 seq=456 reason=ctx_switch
```

devon: Which exact versions? driver, cuda inside container, and nsys?

sam: nsys 2024.5.1, driver 535.86, container CUDA 12.2 (image we build in CI). Host CUDA driver is 535.86. We recently rolled host driver from 520->535 a week ago.

maria: Two common things to check: 1) is libcupti in the container (or mounted from host)? 2) are capabilities / seccomp preventing proper CUPTI init so nsys falls back to sampling causing weird behavior?

sam: I inspected the container — libcupti.so was missing (we use slim image). nsys still runs but warns about CUPTI and uses an alternate instrument mode. We also saw repeated context create/destroy in our app traces.

lee: Mounting CUPTI from host into container often fixes the "CUPTI not initialized" case. Try: 
```
-v /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:ro \
-e LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH 
```
That gives nsys access to the matching libcupti for the driver.

devon: Also note driver 535 contains some cuBLAS heuristic changes. If different cuBLAS kernels are chosen because of slight changes in workspace or stream/context interplay, you can see performance vary request-to-request. Pinning the driver or cuBLAS version on a node could be needed until NVIDIA confirms a regression.

sam: After mounting CUPTI from the host and re-running nsys the timeline changed: CUPTI initialized properly and the kernel variant selection stabilized (only the fast kernel observed). Preliminary perf back to normal in one node.

sam: KV cache issue still puzzling — timeline shows kvcache entries evicted right after a process-level context switch event. snippet: 
```
KVCache: insert key=chat-789 size=12KB ctx=0x7f2a
KVCache: evict key=chat-456 size=10KB reason=ctx_destroy ctx=0x7f2a
cuCtxDestroy_v2 ctx=0x7f2a
```
Suggests our serving process may be creating short-lived CUDA contexts per request in some codepath (legacy fallback), which causes cached per-context allocation to be invalidated.

maria: Can you grep for cuCtxCreate/cuCtxDestroy in the runtime? Also check CUDARuntime vs CUDAManager path — we added a new path last quarter that uses ephemeral contexts for isolation on Dedicated nodes.

sam: Yup — found a code path that does temporary contexts for the fallback path. Will push a small change to reuse the primary context.

devon: For the short term, add a CI check: run nsys smoke profile on our unit test harness with CUPTI available and verify kernel names are stable across 10 runs. If we detect >1 kernel variant for the same matmul op, fail the job and warn.

infra-bot: Created infra ticket: INFRA-2241 to add CUPTI mount to runtime images and a pinned-driver preflight check for Dedicated pools.

lee: One more note — attaching to running containers can be blocked by seccomp/ptrace restrictions. If anyone on this thread tries to reproduce and nsys fails to attach, try relaxing seccomp or run container with --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE for the debug job.

sam: Plan of action:
- immediate workaround: mount host CUPTI and pin driver in the affected pool, add LD_LIBRARY_PATH in smoke image.
- short-term code fix: reuse primary CUDA context instead of ephemeral contexts in fallback path.
- mid-term: add CI nsys stability check + a script that validates CUPTI presence and driver compatibility at node boot.
- if reproduced on stock images after this, file a bug with NVIDIA with the nsys timeline and repro.

sam: cc @devon @maria @lee — I'll open a PR for the context fix + add the CUPTI mount to the debug image and link the profile tarball in the ticket. :thumbsup:
